Subject: Observed duplicate tokens / bill spike with prefetch enabled

Hi Logan / Marissa —

Quick heads-up from our engineering team: since enabling the prefetch optimization last week we started seeing a small number of duplicated downstream generation requests which is materializing as a token-cost spike (10–15% on peak flows). We traced a few sessions and saw repeated prefix generations when a streaming client reconnects while prefetch is inflight.

Attached is a tarball with a trace capture and a short drv log (prefetch-debug.tar.gz). We can reproduce locally and have a short recording on Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D-prefetch-traces

We need two things:
- A short-term way to opt our account out of prefetch while you triage (we're sensitive to cost spikes during Q1).
- A longer-term ask: is there an SDK flag or server-side feature gate you can flip per-tenant so we don't need a client patch in prod?

Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

—Sofia

On Sat, Mar 4, 2028 at 09:34 Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Grace — can you confirm feasibility for a per-tenant runtime flag that disables prefetch and how fast we can ship it as a targeted change for D-8421?

Quick technical summary from runtime: we dug into the traces. Root cause appears to be a race between the prefetch pipeline and streaming-session reconnect handling. When a streaming client drops and reconnects quickly, prefetch can replay a prefix generation while the KV cache hasn't been reconciled, producing effectively duplicate token generation on the same logical user session.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Server-side per-tenant opt-out (recommended short-term): minimal risk, can be implemented as a configuration check before scheduling prefetch work. We can gate it behind account metadata and flip it for Vernix in a single deploy. ETA: 48–72 hours (includes rollout to canary + monitoring).
- Canary rollout of a prefetch debounce (slower): requires a small change to scheduling logic and careful telemetry, ETA ~1 week.
- SDK-side workaround: expose client flag to disable prefetch. This requires Vernix to patch and redeploy their SDK usage; not acceptable if they need immediate relief.

Requesting logs: the tarball is helpful but we need a short snippet with the session id and timestamps for two failing sessions (trace-snippet.txt would be ideal). If Vernix can share those two session ids we can map logs to runtime traces and validate the fix in canary.

I'll coordinate a PR for the server-side opt-out. Grace — can you help with adding the account-level config and run the canary?

-Karthik
